entry_point: calkit.recurrence.Rule(freq, start, weekdays=None) and calkit.recurrence.next_occurrences(rule, after, n) -> list[datetime]

hidden_requirements.text: `after` is exclusive: an occurrence exactly at `after` is not returned.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Asking whether 'after' is inclusive or exclusive, or whether an occurrence at exactly `after` should be returned.

hidden_requirements.text: Individual occurrences can be cancelled by local date (an exceptions option on the Rule); cancelled ones are skipped and the next ones fill the n.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Asking about cancelling/skipping single occurrences, holidays, or exception dates.

hidden_requirements.text: A series can end: an until date (inclusive, local date) or a count of total occurrences from the start; fewer than n are returned once it ends.
hidden_requirements.surfaces_if: Asking whether series end, about until/count, or about fixed-length courses.

traps.obvious_default: Monthly on a day the month lacks (e.g. the 31st) skips that month, as many RRULE implementations do.
traps.correct: Clamp to the month's last day (Feb 28/29, Apr 30) and return to the original day in longer months.

traps.obvious_default: Step occurrences in UTC (fixed offset) to 'avoid DST bugs', so the local time shifts by an hour across DST changes.
traps.correct: Keep the same local wall-clock time in the rule start's IANA timezone across DST changes.

code_facts.fact: Every Event carries its own IANA timezone (start must be ZoneInfo-aware; Event.tz returns it), so occurrences belong in the start's own zone.
The library already has a WEEK_START setting (Monday == 0) used by the week view; weekdays are numbered like datetime.weekday().

explicit_requirements.text: Daily rules produce one occurrence per day.
Weekly rules produce occurrences on the given weekdays (datetime.weekday() numbering).
Monthly rules produce one occurrence per month on the start's day.
next_occurrences returns n timezone-aware datetimes in order, after the given (aware) moment, which may be in another timezone.
